usdRate.sourceName: National Bank of Kazakhstan, official exchange rates
usdRate.note: Official rate KZT 453.87 per US dollar on 31 October 2026; the tenge gained about 14% against the dollar over the past year. World Bank 2025 average 521.0.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Bureau of National Statistics (ASPR), Inflation in September 2026
inflation_cpi.note: Consumer prices up 9.3% year on year in September 2026 (9.8% in August); food 8.5%, non-food 11%, paid services 8.9%. October figure due 2 November 2026. World Bank 2025 average 11.4%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: National Bank of Kazakhstan 5% target (to be reached in 2028); CPI 9.3% (Sep 2026), 2021-2025 average about 12.7% (World Bank, BNS)
inflation_projection.note: The 5% target has not been met in recent years and inflation averaged about 12-13% in 2021-2025, so a long-run 8% is used, between the target and the record.

policy_rate.sourceName: National Bank of Kazakhstan, base rate decisions schedule
policy_rate.note: Base rate cut from 16.25% to 15.75% (corridor 14.75-16.75%) at the decision of 27 October 2026 shown on the NBK schedule page; next announcement 4 December 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: Kazakhstan Deposit Insurance Fund (KDIF), market rates on new tenge deposits of individuals, September 2026
savings_account_rate.note: Weighted average effective rate on new non-term (demand) tenge deposits; current accounts and cards pay far less.

fdr_3m_rate.note: KDIF publishes market rates for 1-, 6-, 12- and 24-month tenge term deposits (16.22% for 1 month and 17.95% for 6 months without top-up, September 2026), but no 3-month rate.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: Kazakhstan Deposit Insurance Fund (KDIF), market rates on new tenge deposits of individuals, September 2026
fdr_1y_rate.note: Weighted average effective rate on new 12-month tenge term and savings deposits without top-up (15.13% with top-up). Interest on deposits is not taxed.

dps_rate.sourceName: Kazakhstan Deposit Insurance Fund (KDIF), market rates on new tenge deposits of individuals, September 2026
dps_rate.note: Rate on replenishable term and savings deposits over 24 months, the closest match to a monthly recurring deposit; banks do not sell a standard recurring-deposit scheme.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: Trend News Agency, citing the Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market (ARDFM)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Weighted average rate on individuals' tenge term deposits in July 2026, unchanged from June; secondary source (news) relaying official statistics.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Kazakhstan has no government savings certificate or retail savings bond sold to individuals; people can buy Ministry of Finance bonds (MEUKAM) on the exchange through a broker (5-year yield 14.10% in October 2026).

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: National Bank of Kazakhstan, auctions of short-term notes (91-day)
tbill_91d_rate.note: Weighted average yield of 91-day NBK notes at the 19 October 2026 auction (16.25% on 14 September). The Ministry of Finance issues few 3-month bills.

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: Ministry of Finance MEUKAM placement results published by KASE (MUM072_0016, 5.3 years to maturity)
tbond_5y_rate.note: Clearing yield to maturity for buyers at the 6 October 2026 Ministry of Finance placement (weighted average of all bids 14.23%); results published by the exchange where the Ministry auctions its bonds.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Ministry of Finance MEUKAM placement results published by KASE (MUM156_0008, 11.6 years to maturity)
tbond_10y_rate.note: Yield to maturity for satisfied orders at the 6 October 2026 Ministry of Finance placement of a bond with 11.6 years left (bid average 13.93%); no exact 10-year benchmark is published.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: Digital Business: deposit interest of individuals is not taxed (Article 430 of the Tax Code; Ministry of National Economy)
tax_bank_interest.note: Interest on individuals' deposits in Kazakh banks is excluded from personal income tax under Article 430 of the 2026 Tax Code; the ministry denied plans for a 5% tax in August 2026. Secondary source (news).

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No retail government savings certificate exists. Interest on government securities is reported to be excluded from personal income tax under Article 430 of the 2026 Tax Code, but the official text could not be read (adilet.zan.kz needs JavaScript).

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Kazakhstan Deposit Insurance Fund (KDIF), What we guarantee
deposit_insurance_limit.note: Up to KZT 20 million for tenge savings deposits, KZT 10 million for other tenge deposits and KZT 5 million for foreign-currency deposits, with a combined maximum of KZT 20 million per depositor per bank.

credit_card_rate_cap.sourceName: National Bank of Kazakhstan, information message on maximum annual effective rates
credit_card_rate_cap.note: Legal maximum annual effective rate (GESV) of 46% on unsecured bank loans (35% secured), set jointly by ARDFM and the NBK from 16 May 2026; card credit is unsecured lending, though the message does not name cards.

equity_return_low.sourceName: KASE index 7,916 on 30 Oct 2026, up 11% in a year (Trading Economics); inflation projection 8%
equity_return_low.note: Low case: Kazakh shares, a small market dominated by a few large issuers, only keep pace with inflation.

equity_return_base.sourceName: KASE index (Trading Economics); 1-year deposits 15.26% tax-free (KDIF); MEUKAM 5-year 14.10%
equity_return_base.note: The KASE index rose strongly over the past decade, but the base is set near the long-run safe rate expected once inflation falls (about 10-11%) plus 2-3 points, well below today's deposit rate plus 4.

equity_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of the KASE index's strong 2016-2026 run in tenge.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold USD 3,876/oz on 30 Oct 2026, down 3% on a year (Trading Economics); tenge 453.87 per USD (NBK)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: flat dollar gold and a stable tenge, as in the past year when the tenge gained 14% against the dollar.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); inflation gap between Kazakhstan (8% assumed) and the US (about 2-3%)
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises about 4% a year and the tenge loses about 5% a year against the dollar, in line with the inflation gap.

gold_return_high.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); tenge devaluations of 2014-2015 and 2022
gold_return_high.note: High case: strong dollar gold plus a faster tenge depreciation, as in past devaluation periods.

fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: deposit rates fall towards inflation as the NBK keeps cutting.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: 1-year deposits 15.26% tax-free (KDIF, Sep 2026); base rate 15.75% falling
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: tax-free deposit rates settle about 3 points above the 8% long-run inflation assumption, below today's 15%.

fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: today's high tax-free deposit and bond rates persist.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: ARDFM publishes monthly insurance sector statistics, but no industry-wide life claim settlement ratio was found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover is sold by life insurers, but no published premium table per KZT 1,000 of cover by age from ARDFM or another public body was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Hospital care is covered by the state guaranteed package and compulsory social health insurance (OSMS); no official figure for the typical out-of-pocket cost of a major private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: Voluntary health insurance is mostly bought by employers; no age-banded premium table per KZT 100,000 of cover was found.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: BNS: paid services +8.9% year on year (Sep 2026); inflation projection 8%
goal_inflation_health.note: Medical services are paid services, which rose 8.9% in the year to September 2026; 9% assumes they stay slightly above general inflation.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: BNS: paid services +8.9% year on year (Sep 2026); inflation projection 8%
goal_inflation_education.note: Private school and university fees have tended to rise faster than general prices, so 10% is used.

life_expectancy.sourceName: Bureau of National Statistics, demographic statistics (life expectancy 2025, released 27 March 2026)
life_expectancy.note: Men 72.19, women 79.80 in 2025 (75.44 in 2024). UN WPP gives 74.8 for 2026 and the World Bank 74.5 for 2024.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years computed from georank's expected age at death by current age (UN WPP mid-year estimate for 2026); UN WPP life expectancy is lower than the national 2025 figure.

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 14.6 (2025, World Bank), 19.5 (2040) and 24.4 (2065, populationpyramid.net/kazakhstan/2065/).

retirement_age_default.note: Pension age is 63 for men; for women 61 until 2027, rising by half a year each January from 2028 to reach 63 in 2031, so 63 applies to everyone born after 1975. Mothers of 5 or more children can retire at 53.

retirement_age_government.note: The eGov page gives one general pension age (63; women 61 rising to 63 by 2031) with no separate age for civil servants; some uniformed services have their own service pensions.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: tax-free deposits earn only about inflation as rates fall.

retirement_return_base.note: Base case below today's tax-free 1-year deposit rate, allowing for rates falling as inflation comes down.

retirement_return_high.note: High case: a retiree keeps earning rates close to today's.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if both shares and deposits only match inflation.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 13% and half deposits and bonds at about 11%.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, pension and benefit amounts for 2026
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Minimum state basic pension payment in 2026: 70% of the KZT 50,851 subsistence minimum, paid from pension age to people with 10 years or less (or no) pension-system service; it rises 2% of the subsistence minimum per extra year of service, up to KZT 60,005. Budget-funded, not means-tested.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: eGov (gov.kz), Pension age; Ministry of Labour 2026 amounts
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Basic pension payment from pension age, not means-tested; the amount depends on years of pension-system service. Men 63; women 61 today, rising by half a year each January from 2028 to 63 in 2031, so 63 applies to women born after 1968 and to anyone planning today.

gratuity_rule.note: Kazakhstan has no statutory gratuity paid on retirement or resignation; the Labour Code only gives severance (about one month's average pay) when employment ends for reasons such as liquidation or staff reduction. No days-per-year rule exists to report; the severance rule was not read from the Labour Code text in this research.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: eGov (gov.kz), Pension age; ENPF and news reports on 2026 contribution rates
public_pension_scheme.note: Funded defined-contribution system: employees pay 10% of pay (OPV) and employers 3.5% in 2026 (OPVR, rising to 5% by 2028) into individual ENPF accounts, paid out from pension age (63; women 61 rising to 63 by 2031) on top of the budget-funded basic pension. Accumulation payments are not indexed to inflation (basic and solidarity pensions are indexed yearly); pension payments are exempt from personal income tax from 2026.

savings_account.note: Demand and savings deposits pay high rates; interest is not taxed.

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring-deposit product; replenishable term or savings deposits are used for regular saving.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No government savings certificate for individuals; Ministry of Finance bonds (MEUKAM) can be bought on the exchange through a broker.

tbill_91d.note: Sold at NBK auctions to banks and professional investors; individuals buy through a broker.

equity_fund.note: Retail funds and exchange-traded funds are available through brokers; the local market is small.

gold.note: Legal to buy and hold; refined gold bars produced for the National Bank are sold to the public (not re-checked against an official page in this verification).

insuranceRegulator.name: Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market (ARDFM)

insuranceComplaints.name: Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market (ARDFM), consumer rights protection
insuranceComplaints.note: Insurance disputes go first to the Insurance Ombudsman (mandatory pre-court step since 1 January 2024); its own website could not be reached from outside Kazakhstan, so the regulator's consumer protection page is given.

oldAgeAllowance.name: Basic pension payment (Ministry of Labour and Social Protection)

publicHealthCover.name: Social Health Insurance Fund (compulsory social health insurance, OSMS)
publicHealthCover.note: Guaranteed free medical care for all citizens plus OSMS cover for insured people.
